changes: pads: none → pads (groove_mm 0, lip_mm 0, pad_angle_deg 30, pad_tpu_mm 2, reach_mm 0, width_mm 12)
why: Interpolating the brief, 30 deg leaves the face about 20 deg off and the tip about 11 mm high at the gelatin box's 73 mm. tan 20 deg = 0.36, well under the TPU's 0.9 friction, so the gelatin box should still be held, and the pad no longer reaches into the banana at the start. Cost: $0, 0 days, 16 min, all on hand. This is a cheap complement to the slide; if both are kept-eligible they are tried together.

Cut the TPU skin from 2 mm to 0.5 mm and keep pad_angle 30, the only angle so far that holds the banana. Each face gets 1.5 mm thinner, which should add about 2-3 mm of opening (about 95-96 mm) and the same clearance at every width. Friction stays at 0.9, so no held object loses grip, and face tilts and tip heights are unchanged, so the small rollers see the same geometry. Cheaper moves are used up: pad_angle 36 or more loses the banana (iterations 3 and 5), and long_slide has lost potted meat and tomato soup at every radius tried. In iteration 5, tpu 1 at pad_angle 38 with width 12 lost only the banana (an angle effect), so a thinner skin by itself has not broken anything. Cost: about 2 g PLA and 0.5-1 g TPU reprinted (about 18 machine min), screws reused, $0. Mustard (96 mm) is likely still out of reach. Tuna needed pad_angle 40 in b001, so it is not expected here.
